## Accepted Article

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Accepted</span></p>
<h3>The spatial structure and influencing factors of the flow of global top biomedical scientists from the perspective of urban network</h3>

Role: First Author. Accepted by *World Regional Studies*.

This article examines the mobility trajectories of top global biomedical scientists from an urban-network perspective. It compares education and employment stages and analyzes city-level factors associated with scientist mobility.

[View details →](papers/urban-network-biomedical-mobility.html){.publication-link}

## Submitted Manuscripts

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Submitted Manuscript</span></p>
<h3>Structure and Formation Mechanisms of the Intercity Mobility Network of Top Global Biomedical Scientists: A Dual Whole-Network and Ego-Network Perspective</h3>

Role: First Author.

This manuscript links whole-network mobility structures with individual ego-network trajectories. It examines how urban conditions, multidimensional proximity, platform histories, and prior ties shape intercity mobility among top biomedical scientists.

[View details →](papers/whole-ego-mobility.html){.publication-link}
:::

::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Submitted Manuscript</span></p>
<h3>Pre-move coauthor ties and the direction of scientific mobility: A city-level choice analysis of highly cited biomedical scientists</h3>

Role: First Author.

This manuscript treats intercity employment moves as event-specific destination choices. It compares selected cities with candidate alternatives and tests whether pre-move direct coauthor ties help distinguish scientists' destinations.

[View details →](papers/pre-move-coauthor-ties.html){.publication-link}
:::
:::

## Selected Research Outputs

::: {.output-list .editorial-list}
::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Selected Research Output</span></p>
<h3>Comparative Study on Biomedical Innovation between China and the United States from the Perspective of Talent Mobility Network</h3>

Role: First Author.

This study compares biomedical innovation in China and the United States through the mobility networks of top scientists. It relates talent movement to innovation systems, research output, patents, and innovation transformation.

[View details →](papers/china-us-biomedical-innovation.html){.publication-link}
:::

::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Selected Research Output</span></p>
<h3>Assessment of urban resilience based on nighttime light remote sensing and Fisher's information method</h3>

Role: First Author.

This study uses nighttime-light data and Fisher Information Light to evaluate short-term urban resilience during the COVID-19 shock. It compares resilience trajectories across 48 cities in three major Chinese urban agglomerations.

[View details →](papers/urban-resilience-nighttime-lights.html){.publication-link}
:::

::: {.output-item}
<p><span class="status-badge">Selected Research Output</span></p>
<h3>Analysis on the spatial-temporal evolution of global trade network in the context of the COVID-19</h3>

Role: First Author.

This study analyzes changes in the global commodity trade network from 2019 to 2021. It compares network structure across countries, regions, and product types under the COVID-19 shock.

[View details →](papers/global-trade-network.html){.publication-link}
:::
